# Yakkha Saṁyutta (SN 10)

**ID:** SN 10
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Yakkha Saṁyutta
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0301m.mul9.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

All twelve discourses have parallels identified in the Chinese Āgamas, specifically eleven suttas each corresponding to discourses in the *Bieyi za ahan jing* (T 100 / SA2) and the *Za ahan jing* (T 99 / SĀ), an alignment substantiated by DharmaNexus's cross-language matches [DharmaNexus]. Textual comparison with the Chinese parallel SA2 326 has notably helped resolve the reading of the nun's name in SN 10.11 as Vīrā or Cīrā [Bingenheimer, Studies in Agama Literature]. Furthermore, Pali-internal text reuse is significant: SN 10.12 and SN 10.3 correspond directly to the *Āḷavaka Sutta* (Snp 1.10) and *Sūciloma Sutta* (Snp 2.5) of the *Suttanipāta* [DharmaNexus]. Extended segments—especially from the Sudatta episode in SN 10.8—are also shared with the Vinaya's *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16) and are aligned by DharmaNexus with the Sanskrit *Śayanāsanavastu* and *Saṅghabhedavastu*, as well as Tibetan Vinaya and *Udānavarga* texts [DharmaNexus].
